sentences.text: Shri Arjun Pathak - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Santosh Singh Thakur Ga for the State.
 Order

This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. Act, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 114 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Chandravatiganj, Indore, District- Indore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 365, 328.
376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 12/11/2024.

As per the case of prosecution, husband of the prosecutrix reported to PS- Chandravati Ganj, Indore (Rural) on 03/02/2024 that his wife aged around 30 years along with younger son is missing since afternoon of 02/02/2024.
The prosecutrix appeared before PS- Chandrawani Ganj on 10/11/2024.
She alleged that her relative Naresh (applicant) used to communicate with her.
Naresh was not happy with his married life.
On 03/02/2024 around 12:34 hours, she went to Bherunath temple with her younger son.
Naresh offered them a cake on the pretext of celebrating NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:787 2 MCRC-54950-2024 birthday.
She and her son went unconscious after consuming the cake.
Naresh took them to remote place and threatened to kill them.
Naresh confined them in a rented room and committed rape on her on multiple occasions.
On 09/11/2024, she got opportunity and escaped with her son.
She went to her matrimonial home at Village- Khalkhala and informed her parents.
On such allegation, PS- Chandravatiganj registered FIR at Crime no. 114 of 2024 for the offence punishable under sections 328, 365, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC against Naresh (applicant).
The statements of the prosecutrix were recorded under sections 180 and 183 of BNSS, 2023.

sentences.text: It was informed that Naresh was working as a labourer and the lady and her son stayed at home.
The applicant was arrested on 12/11/2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On complication of investigation, final report was submitted.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
contends that the applicant is falsely implicated in this matter.
It is a case of consensual relationship between two adults.
The prosecutrix had left her matrimonial home along with minor son and came to live with the applicant.
When their relationship turned sour, false allegations of rape have been leveled against the applicant.
No offence as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
The prosecutrix has stayed for almost nine months with the applicant, thereafter, she left him and lodged the report.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 37 years and is an agriculturist by profession.

There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:787 3 MCRC-54950-2024 his home, family and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence by the applicant as both the parties relate to similar socio-economic status.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of the alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant- Naresh s hall be released on bail in connection with the Crime as stated in para - 1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount,
as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court/the Committal Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C., 1973/Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the concerned Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:787 4 MCRC-54950-2024 The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules
